# Engine build inputs (WebAssembly)

Files preserved from the packaging research (`wiki/rust-engine.md`, section 7) so the `wasm32-wasip1` build of the `pg_query` crate (libpg_query inside) is reproducible:

- `pg_query-18.0.0.patch`: the diff against `pg_query` 18.0.0, the Postgres 18 parser. That version is not on crates.io yet, so `engine/build.sh --prepare` fetches it from GitHub by commit and checks each archive against a SHA-256: [pganalyze/pg_query.rs](https://github.com/pganalyze/pg_query.rs) at `ad0c87ed`, the head of the branch `pg-18` on 2026-10-11 (pull request 79, "Release 18.0.0"), and the libpg_query commit its submodule names, `c1546e7e`, which is the tag 18.1.0 and the grammar of Postgres 18.6. Two hunks are for WebAssembly: the `build.rs` change that pastes in the `extern "C"` block bindgen drops on wasm targets, and that block (`pg_query-extern_block.rs` is the block, 36 functions captured from a native build's bindings; `pg_query-build.rs` is the full patched `build.rs`). Four are for every target, and fix libpg_query where no release of `pg_query` has the fix yet: two in `libpg_query/src/pg_query.c` make the key that frees a thread's memory context once for the process rather than once in every thread that parses, which used up the process's keys after `PTHREAD_KEYS_MAX` such threads (the engine parses on a thread of its own for each call); and two in `libpg_query/src/pg_query_json_plpgsql.c` dump a trigger function's `PLPGSQL_DTYPE_PROMISE` datums (`tg_op` and the rest), whose JSON was otherwise invalid, and a `RETURN`'s `retvarno`, without which `RETURN new` and `RETURN old` dump the same. The rest make the copy a crate of its own, `reylo-pg-query`, which Reylo's crates depend on and which publishes to crates.io: its manifest's name, license and `include` (with the licenses and `extern_block.rs`), and a `links` key whose `root`, printed by `build.rs`, is the crate's directory, where the engine's build script reads libpg_query's headers and node definitions; and `build.rs` regenerates `src/protobuf.rs` only when `REGENERATE_PROTOBUF` asks, never because `protoc` is installed, so that a build from crates.io writes nothing into its package. How deeply a statement may nest is the engine's own bound, which `src/raw.rs` holds the tree it reads to (`src/stack.rs`), so the patch leaves libpg_query's depth and stack limits as they are. The two commits and their SHA-256s are in `pg_query-source.sh`, which `build.sh` reads, so that a new one changes the engine's fingerprint. When crates.io has 18.0.0, they give way to the crate's version and the patch stays as it is. Until 2026-10-11 the patch was `pg_query-6.2.0-wasm.patch`, against crates.io's 6.2.0 (Postgres 17), with the first two parts alone.
- `stubs/`: the headers libpg_query includes and WASI does not provide (`syslog.h`, `netdb.h`), and `wasi_extra.h`, which `build.sh` includes into every C file: it defines `EHOSTDOWN` and maps `sigsetjmp` and `siglongjmp` to `setjmp` and `longjmp`. Postgres 18's parser needed no new one.

Toolchain: `wasi-sdk` 34 (`CC` and `AR` from its `bin/`, `--sysroot` from its `share/wasi-sysroot`, `-I stubs`), `rustup target add wasm32-wasip1`, `cargo build --release --target wasm32-wasip1`.
